solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stylish US player revealing beam making return

parts.note: fly is slang for smart or stylish
a back is a position in American football

explanation.surface: A fashionable American sportsman shows off some move that brings him back.
explanation.walkthrough: In a cathode-ray tube the electron beam sweeps across the screen and then snaps back to start the next line; that snap back is the flyback.
explanation.definitionFit: Flyback is the technical term for the rapid return sweep of the scanning electron beam in a television tube.

clue.text: Sailor's first misbehaving, having beak agape

indicators.note: letters that misbehave will not keep to their proper order

parts.note: all twelve letters used as printed

explanation.surface: A sailor was the first to behave badly, and stood gaping open-mouthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks like it should select an initial letter, but every letter of the two words is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fissirostral describes birds such as swifts with a deeply cleft, wide-gaping bill, from Latin fissus split and rostrum beak.

clue.text: Run away to Scotland? Most tear northwards, filled with love

indicators.note: most of a word means all of it bar the last letter
in a down entry going northwards means reading from the bottom up
something filled with another thing has it placed inside

parts.note: pull, as in tear along, loses its final letter
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone flees north to Scotland, weeping and full of love.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'to Scotland' flag a Scots word: loup is Scots for leap, and also to run away.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect loup means to leap or spring, and by extension to flee or bolt, so it is a Scottish word for run away.

clue.text: Affliction of starving kid tucking into edible root, one forest-dweller

indicators.note: a thing tucking into food goes inside it

parts.note: the yam is a starchy edible tuber
noma is a gangrenous disease of the mouth and face, mostly in malnourished children
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A disease of a hungry child makes its way into the root vegetable that feeds a jungle family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of starving kid' is not wordplay but description: noma strikes chiefly malnourished children, which tells the solver which affliction is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yanomami are an indigenous people living in the Amazon rainforest on the Brazil–Venezuela border.

clue.text: Crude report we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word's sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a bruit is a rumour or report, said like broot

explanation.surface: Someone describes a rough account they have been told.
explanation.definitionFit: Brute as an adjective means coarse, raw or unrefined, as in brute force, close to crude.

clue.text: Forgotten oriental ravine with earth at the bottom

parts.note: a chine is a narrow coastal ravine, as on the Isle of Wight
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: An Eastern traveller lies lost and forgotten in a gully with soil heaped on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the bottom' tells you the earth comes last in this down entry. 'Forgotten' marks the answer as an obsolete word, a dated and now offensive term.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinee is an archaic, now derogatory, word for a Chinese person, hence an obsolete term for someone from the Orient.

clue.text: What's pelt covering start of rain soaks dreadfully

indicators.note: one thing covering another wraps around it
done dreadfully means done badly, the letters left in a mess

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of rain

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why an animal skin over a raindrop gets so drenched.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaross is a South African cloak or rug made from animal skins, so it is literally something made of pelt.

clue.text: Seaweed left in bed

indicators.note: something in another thing sits inside it

parts.note: kip is slang for a bed or sleep
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Some kelp has been left lying on a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilp is an old variant spelling of kelp, the large brown seaweed.

clue.text: King presiding over tribe, one in NZ

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
iwi is the Maori word for a tribe

explanation.surface: A chief rules his people, a figure in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presiding over' places the king first, on top in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiwi is the everyday nickname for a New Zealander, as well as the country's flightless national bird.

clue.text: A tie's broken, nothing left within — separate

indicators.note: within means placed inside the other letters
something broken has its parts scattered out of order

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like O
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A drawn match is overturned with no score remaining, so the teams are split.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to set something apart from others, a verb synonym of separate.

clue.text: Pluto e.g. producing high-pitched cry, a row

parts.note: a pipe is a shrill, high note, as of a bird
a row of things is a line

explanation.surface: The dwarf planet, or perhaps the cartoon dog, lets out a squeal while lined up.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto is not the planet or Disney's dog: PLUTO (Pipe-Line Under The Ocean) carried fuel across the English Channel after D-Day in 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: Operation PLUTO laid undersea fuel pipes to supply Allied armies in France, so Pluto is an example of a pipeline.

clue.text: One converts flats regularly, rentin' space variously around Spain

indicators.note: letters going around another sit on either side of it
variously means in various ways, so the letters take a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, dropped g and all
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A landlord routinely turns apartments into lets, renting out space in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flats' are not apartments but the painted canvas panels of theatre scenery; 'regularly' belongs to the definition, not a letter-picking signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene painter in a theatre routinely paints the flat canvas frames of stage scenery, turning them into settings.

clue.text: Antiquated backless couch chucked in lorry

indicators.note: without its back means the final letter is lost
something chucked in a vehicle ends up inside it

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry
a chaise (longue) is a couch, here losing its last letter

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned sofa without a backrest is thrown into a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backless' looks like a description of furniture, but it removes the final letter; a lorry is a British truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaistic means imitating the archaic, deliberately old-fashioned in style, which is close to antiquated.

clue.text: Dawn offering broth, abandoning love for one

indicators.note: abandoning one thing for another swaps the first out and the second in

parts.note: broth is a kind of soup
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
'un is a dialect form of one, as in a good 'un

explanation.surface: Someone serves soup at daybreak, leaving a lover for a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is the moment the sun rises, an American-flavoured synonym for dawn or sunrise.

clue.text: Pitcher some deployed from the rear

indicators.note: read from the rear means read back to front
some of a word means only part of its letters

parts.note: four letters sitting inside the word

explanation.surface: A baseball pitcher is brought on from the back of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitcher' suggests baseball but is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: An olpe is an ancient Greek jug with a round body and handle, used for pouring wine or oil.

clue.text: Inhabitant bagging trophy, exactly as required

indicators.note: something bagging another has captured it inside

parts.note: Chambers gives son as a native or inhabitant, as in sons of the soil
a pot is slang for a cup or trophy

explanation.surface: A local wins the cup, which is precisely what was needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is British informal for absolutely accurate or perfect, which is precisely what was required.

clue.text: Fuel extractors abandoned most of old mine

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter
abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, letters let loose from their order

parts.note: old without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drillers walked away from nearly all of a disused pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilmen work in the petroleum industry, drilling and pumping oil, a fuel, from the ground.

clue.text: Sadden old prisoner, time including wretched stir

indicators.note: something wretched is in a sorry, disordered state

parts.note: con is short for convict
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former convict depresses us, serving time in a miserable jail (stir being slang for prison).
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is British slang for prison, which makes it look like a definition rather than letters to rearrange; 'old' marks the answer as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrist is an obsolete verb meaning to make sorrowful, from Latin contristare, so it is an old word for sadden.

clue.text: The emptied barn, open to examination

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the
a stable is a farm building for horses

explanation.surface: The barn is cleared out and thrown open for inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something testable can be checked or tried, which is what being open to examination means.

clue.text: Great novelist, first of three — one partner's not enough for him

definitions.text: one partner's not enough for him

parts.note: big means great in size
Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists

indicators.note: the first of a word is only its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of three

explanation.surface: A celebrated writer, the first of a trio, is a man who cannot make do with one wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Martin Amis's three-novel trilogy, but the novelist simply supplies the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamist marries a second spouse while still married to the first, so one partner is clearly too few for him.

clue.text: Wherein you'd find Toad, rest appalled! (8, two words)

definitions.text: Wherein you'd find Toad, rest appalled!

indicators.note: appalled pictures shock and disarray, which leaves the letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is out in a motor car, and everyone else is horrified.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: Toad's reckless motoring trials would horrify the rest of the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A road test is a trial drive of a vehicle on public roads, exactly where the motor-mad Toad would be found.

clue.text: He hung about women often left in peril

indicators.note: something in another thing is placed inside it

parts.note: peril is danger
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A man who loitered around women frequently left them in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as a verb in the surface but is the abbreviation for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers defines a dangler as one who dangles about or hangs around women, a dated term for a would-be suitor.

clue.text: He may have splurged magenta round third of canvas

definitions.text: He may have splurged magenta round third of canvas

indicators.note: splurged paint is splashed about freely, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the third of a word is its third letter alone

parts.note: third letter of canvas

explanation.surface: A painter slaps a bright pink-purple colour round a canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition, and the whole clue describes what a painter might do; 'round' places the canvas letter inside the reshuffled colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Mantegna was a fifteenth-century Italian Renaissance painter, so he might well have splashed colour on canvas.

clue.text: Sailor is still climbing in manoeuvre using double rope

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: something that lies is staying still

explanation.surface: A sailor is still clambering up the rigging during a rope exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is still' reads as 'continues to be' but means remains motionless; 'climbing' paradoxically sends the letters upward in a descent manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a cliff by sliding down a doubled rope fixed above, a mountaineering manoeuvre.

clue.text: Nod head aiming for heart of agreement

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
aiming for something is aiming at it

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: Someone nods their head, trying for the core of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nutate is to nod, from Latin nutare; botanists also use it for a plant tip swaying.

clue.text: Smelly insect intertwines back to irritate (8, two words)

indicators.note: going back means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to knit is to intertwine yarn
to bug someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: An odorous creature knots itself around and gets on your nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: The stink bug, or shield bug, gives off a foul odour when threatened, so it is a smelly insect by name.

clue.text: Lecherous acts with nothing on, removing top and bottom?

indicators.note: taking off the top and bottom of a down word drops its first and last letters, keeping the middle

parts.note: togless, without togs (clothes), stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A lustful striptease: someone naked, having taken off both top and bottoms.
explanation.walkthrough: Togs are clothes, so togless means wearing nothing; the question mark nods to the clothes-shedding picture, while the instruction actually trims letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogles are lustful, leering looks, the stares of a lecher, so lecherous acts in noun form.

clue.text: Jock's faith proves heavy going by the sound of it

indicators.note: going by sound means take how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: to trog is to trudge wearily, so heavy going

explanation.surface: A Scotsman finds his religion is hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is the stock nickname for a Scotsman, flagging a Scots word: troggs, a form of troth.
explanation.definitionFit: Troggs is a Scots word for troth or faith, used as a mild oath, so it is a Scotsman's word for faith.

clue.text: Revolver, either end of it penetrating, making one snarl

indicators.note: something penetrating another goes into the middle of it

parts.note: a revolver is a handgun

indicators.note: either end of a word gives its first or last letter, here the same

parts.note: 'it' stands for the word revolver, which begins and ends with the same letter

explanation.surface: A spinning bullet goes in, and the victim grimaces.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolver both begins and ends with R, so either end gives the same letter; 'it' refers back to the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To gurn is to pull a grotesque face or snarl; a gurn is that grimace, famous from Cumbrian gurning contests.

clue.text: Inner coat for those attending sheep?

parts.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year
men are attendants or workers

explanation.surface: A warm layer of clothing for shepherds.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that teg men is an invented name for shepherds; the coat is botanical, not woolly.
explanation.definitionFit: The tegmen is the thin inner layer of a seed's covering, inside the outer testa, so a botanical inner coat.

clue.text: Traces of fugitives seen? Posse reveals opposite of this

indicators.note: traces are faint parts of something, here letters lying across words

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A sheriff's posse spots tracks of escapees going the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: Posse here is the Latin word 'to be able', as in the phrase in posse (potentially), whose contrary is in esse (actually).
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy esse is actual being, contrasted with posse, potential being; Chambers calls it the opposite of posse.

clue.text: Monetary unit that is held in both hands

indicators.note: something held in another is placed inside it

parts.note: right and left, R and L
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone holds cash in both palms.
explanation.definitionFit: The riel is the currency of Cambodia, a national monetary unit.

clue.text: Not the first-rankers, once glorified

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the second tier of celebrities
second meaning: an archaic past participle of bless

explanation.surface: Former stars who are no longer top names.
explanation.walkthrough: Blist is an obsolete form of blessed; the surface suggests faded celebrity, but the second half is an old verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: The B-list holds second-rate celebrities, not the A-listers; blist was once the past tense of bless, meaning praised.

clue.text: Rough places I traipse roaming El Salvador

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about with no fixed course

parts.note: taken as written
ES is the international vehicle code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: A backpacker trudges through the rugged terrain of Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperities are roughnesses or rugged spots on a surface, from Latin asper, rough.

clue.text: Fuss-free storm in bits

indicators.note: free of something means rid of it, so those letters go

parts.note: a tornado is a violent storm
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A tempest without bother leaves everything shredded.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn means ripped apart, so something torn is in pieces.

clue.text: One responsible for catalogue including English and Scottish spear

indicators.note: something including another holds it inside

parts.note: a lister is one who draws up a list
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A cataloguer lists English and Scottish weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A leister is a pronged fish-spear used in Scotland, especially for salmon.
